_README: Where task generation should start, per agent model.
Difficulty is defined relative to the agent (measured pass rate + a fixed
band), so nothing about a task predicts how hard it will be for a given
model. But the *node count* of the sampled tool graph does move the whole
distribution, and that is a per-model property: a stronger agent needs a
longer chain before the band stops being empty. This file records the
starting point measured for each model so generation does not have to
re-derive it, and so adding a model is a data edit rather than a code edit.
Model keys are matched case-insensitively against the basename of the
'evidence' is not read by any code. It is there so the next person to
change a number has to look at what the current one was measured on.

Qwen3-8B.evidence: mcp_notes, screened bank: gc=3 n=327 mean=0.703, 65% pinned at 1.00, band yield 9%; gc=4 n=65 mean=0.610, 46% pinned at 1.00, band yield 28%. gc=4 was screened at 3 reps (fewer reps pin more), so its advantage is if anything understated. Caveat: all 65 gc=4 tasks are train-split, so this is observational, not a controlled experiment.

Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B.evidence: NOT MEASURED. Carried over from Qwen3-8B as a placeholder. This model is the simulator, not an agent, in every run so far; screen before trusting this row.
